title: Northgate Credit Cards Account Closure and Reward Forfeiture
content:
Cardholder terms of Northgate Credit Cards on the closing of an account and what becomes of its rewards.

## Clause

Accounts are closed only by Meridian Trust Bank, at the cardholder's request or on its own credit grounds; Northgate member services takes no closure request itself and refers the cardholder to the bank. Where the card's terms provide that rewards are forfeited on closure, a card rewards balance not yet issued is forfeited on the closure date. A forfeiture is booked only on an account whose status is closed. A certificate already issued before the closure stays redeemable until it expires.

## Effects of a closure

| Item | On closure |
|---|---|
| Who closes | Meridian Trust Bank, from active or restricted status |
| Closure date | Recorded on the account |
| Card rewards balance not yet issued | Forfeited on the closure date, where the card's terms so provide, and booked in the reward year in which the account closed |
| Certificate issued before the closure | Stays redeemable until it expires |
| Forfeiture on an account not closed | Not booked; a forfeiture is booked only on a closed account |

## Questions answered (hypothetical accounts)

**A cardholder calls member services asking to close the card. Does member services close it?**
No. Member services takes no closure request itself and refers the cardholder to the bank.

**An account closes on 14 May with $23.40 of rewards earned that year and not yet issued, on a card whose terms forfeit rewards on closure. What happens to the $23.40?**
It is forfeited on 14 May, the closure date.

**The same account received its certificate for the previous reward year in February. Can that certificate still be used?**
Yes. A certificate issued before the closure stays redeemable until it expires.

**Can a forfeiture be booked on an account that is still restricted?**
No. Its status is not closed.
